en: The tamaraw, the national animal of the Philippines, is a dwarf buffalo endemic to the island of Mindoro.
The Philippine eagle, declared the national bird in 1995, has a distinctive crest of dark brown feathers on its head.
The sampaguita, the national flower, is a white jasmine species scientifically known as Jasminum sambac.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect conical shape, which is a result of stratovolcano geological formation.
National hero Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses.
Malacanang Palace, the official residence of the Philippine president, is located along the northern bank of the Pasig River.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces by carving steps into mountains using stone walls and ancient irrigation.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The white equilateral triangle on the Philippine flag represents liberty, equality, and fraternity, designed by Emilio Aguinaldo.
Dr. Fe del Mundo founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines and invented a bamboo incubator.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system that uses fourteen consonants and three vowels to represent syllables.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu celebrates the Santo Nino with a dance mimicking the flow of a river.
